clue.text: Wild horse in EastEnders has to die

indicators.note: EastEnders is a soap set in London's East End, where the Cockney accent drops the opening H of words

blocks.note: 'must' means 'has to'
to hang is to die on the gallows

explanation.surface: A runaway horse turns up in the BBC soap and has to be killed off.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap set in Cockney east London; said the Cockney way, hang loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is the free-roaming feral horse of the American West.

clue.text: A dainty bit to eat – run out for wine

indicators.note: when someone is run out they leave, so the letter is taken away

blocks.note: a morsel is a small tasty mouthful
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A tasty snack has run out, so it is time for the wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' looks like 'used up', but the run is the letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosel is a German white wine named after the river valley where it is made.

clue.text: Use heroin to grow very fast

blocks.note: first meaning: inject a drug, in slang
second meaning: to rise or grow rapidly, as a teenager does

explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies heroin as a growth aid; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb is slang for injecting a drug and also means to grow quickly.

clue.text: Thunderstruck, one day

blocks.note: a means one
Wed is the abbreviation for Wednesday

explanation.surface: Someone left stunned on a single day.
explanation.definitionFit: Being awed means being filled with wonder, dumbfounded as if struck by thunder.

clue.text: Accelerate and foolishly persist in sporty effect

indicators.note: doing something foolishly means doing it without sense or order, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: to accelerate is to go faster
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A boy racer speeds up and stubbornly keeps showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: Go-faster stripes are the decorative stripes painted along a car to make it look fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The stripes are a cosmetic decoration meant to make a car look sporty without improving it.

clue.text: Leaf insect's colourful display

blocks.note: a leaf of a book is a page
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A leaf insect, which mimics foliage, puts on a showy display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaf insect' reads as one creature, but it splits into two pieces; the 's stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a grand public spectacle, often with costumes and processions.

clue.text: No paragon, a stern criminal who may face expulsion

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A stern lawbreaker, far from a model citizen, could be deported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reads as a noun for the wrongdoer, but it is the adjective signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names an unwelcome person, typically a diplomat ordered to leave a country.

clue.text: Feels sad about national party's complaints

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to grieve is to feel sorrow
the ANC is South Africa's African National Congress party

explanation.surface: A political party's grumbles leave someone feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: The ANC, the African National Congress, has governed South Africa since 1994.
explanation.definitionFit: Grievances are formal or felt grounds for complaint about unfair treatment.

clue.text: Our group follows Nurse Bell

blocks.note: a nurse is often called an angel
us is our group

explanation.surface: A team trails behind a nurse named Bell.
explanation.walkthrough: The group piece follows the nurse piece. 'Bell' looks like a surname but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is a Catholic devotion, and also the church bell rung to call people to it.

clue.text: Others hold music to be healing

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside

blocks.note: they means other people
rap is a genre of music

explanation.surface: Some people believe music can cure.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment intended to heal or relieve a disorder.

clue.text: Chosen pen, so fork out

indicators.note: 'out' suggests things put out of their proper order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Having picked a pen, so pay up for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fork out' looks like a phrasal verb meaning pay, but 'out' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoken for is already reserved or claimed by someone, i.e. selected.

clue.text: Fireplace at home, no end of delight

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: being in means being at home
glee is delight

explanation.surface: Sitting by the fire at home brings endless delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' reads as 'plenty of', but it means the last letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is an old word for a hearth or fire burning on it, as in inglenook.

clue.text: Dead on time? Hardly

blocks.note: first meaning: deceased
second meaning: not punctual, arriving after the expected hour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead on time' reads as a phrase for exact punctuality, but 'Dead' is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both someone recently deceased and someone who has missed the appointed hour.

clue.text: Team almost broke into a holiday home

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
going into something puts it inside the other words

blocks.note: taken as written
stony broke means penniless
a villa is a holiday house

explanation.surface: A sports team, nearly skint, breaks into a holiday villa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' looks like the verb of breaking in, but it is the adjective meaning penniless. Aston Villa is a Birmingham football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is an English Premier League football club based in Birmingham.

clue.text: Cheer pilot, manoeuvring this?

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving around, so the letters are shifted into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Applaud the flyer as they steer this aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the aircraft being flown.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue pictures a pilot manoeuvring a rotary-wing aircraft, which is the answer.

clue.text: Football is our world, more or less

blocks.note: first meaning: a ball, a round object
second meaning: the Earth is roughly a ball shape

explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes the fan's claim that football is everything; both halves describe a ball shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A football and the planet are both near-perfect round solid bodies, which is what the word names.

clue.text: Make home in a motor yacht: pardon?

indicators.note: placing one thing in another puts it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
MY is the standard prefix for a motor yacht, as in MY Britannia
to nest is to make a home

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they may live aboard a motor yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes 'pardon' sound like 'excuse me?', but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to a group of offenders.

clue.text: Very high temperatures in an area of sea

blocks.note: first meaning: readings of 40 to 49 degrees Celsius
second meaning: a sea area of the North Sea named in the BBC shipping forecast

explanation.walkthrough: The BBC shipping forecast divides British waters into named areas; this one lies off north-east Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperatures in the forties Celsius are a heatwave, and Forties is a North Sea shipping area.

clue.text: Crab scraping on the roof?

blocks.note: first meaning: a crab with one oversized claw
second meaning: a violinist

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraping' is a jokey word for playing the violin; the musical is Fiddler on the Roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler crab has one huge claw, and the title figure of the musical plays the violin on a rooftop.

clue.text: Get laptop going again to show holiday pictures

blocks.note: a holiday is a rest
pictures are art

explanation.surface: Rebooting a laptop to show friends the holiday snaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart a computer is to reboot it, getting it running once more.

clue.text: Old aristocrat holding new key

indicators.note: holding something means having it within you

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a peer is a noble
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An elderly noble clutches a newly cut key.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is a device for unlocking, and so an opener in the general sense.

clue.text: Summary of long film, almost a long book

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: an epic is a long, grand film
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A synopsis of a long film turning out nearly as long as a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' looks as if it governs the book, but it trims the film.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome can mean an abstract or condensed account, as well as a perfect example.

clue.text: Try to stop how old we are going on record

blocks.note: a record is a vinyl disc
how old we are is our age

explanation.surface: Trying to prevent anyone putting our ages on the record.
explanation.walkthrough: The age piece goes on, i.e. after, the record piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage is to attempt to deter or prevent someone from doing something.

clue.text: Affected by drugs in school?

blocks.note: first meaning: intoxicated, stoned
second meaning: the kind of school, as in the American secondary school

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a pupil on drugs at school; the question mark flags that the second half needs the word to complete 'high school'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means intoxicated and also names the secondary school attended by teenagers.

clue.text: Shade tormented here?

indicators.note: something tormented is twisted in agony, so the letters are wrenched out of order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Is this where a ghost is tortured?
explanation.walkthrough: A shade is a ghost; the whole clue also describes the underworld where the dead suffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades is the Greek underworld, home of the shades of the dead and a byword for hell.

clue.text: Elevated temperature and pressure

blocks.note: first meaning: warmth, hotness
second meaning: intense pressure

explanation.walkthrough: Temperature and pressure sound like a physics pairing, but each is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names hotness and, figuratively, intense strain or coercion on someone.

clue.text: At it, as a minimum

blocks.note: surface reading: someone busy at a task
setter's reading: 'it' stands in for the answer, so 'At' plus the answer is a phrase meaning 'as a minimum'

explanation.walkthrough: Replace 'it' with the answer and the phrase 'at ___' means 'as a minimum'; the answer itself means the smallest amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the smallest amount, and with 'at' before it forms the phrase meaning no fewer than.

clue.text: How many people complete an entire jumbo?

definitions.text: How many people complete an entire jumbo?

blocks.clueFragment: How many people complete an entire jumbo?
blocks.note: surface reading: a riddle about how many people it takes to make up a whole elephant
setter's reading: a jumbo is a jumbo jet, so the answer is the number of passengers filling an airliner

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests an elephant; it is the Boeing 747 jumbo jet.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the full complement of passengers a single aircraft carries.

clue.text: Hope a lot are happy on one's birthday

definitions.text: Hope a lot are happy on one's birthday

blocks.clueFragment: Hope a lot are happy on one's birthday
blocks.note: surface reading: wishing that plenty of guests enjoy a birthday party
setter's reading: 'a lot' is 'many' and 'happy' describes the plural answer, as in the birthday greeting 'Many happy ...'

explanation.walkthrough: The birthday greeting is 'Many happy ___!': the hope is that there will be many happy recurrences of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means recurrences of an annual occasion, as wished in the standard birthday greeting.

clue.text: Naive, like the National Gallery after a heist?

definitions.text: like the National Gallery after a heist?

blocks.note: first meaning: guileless, innocent

blocks.clueFragment: like the National Gallery after a heist?
blocks.note: second meaning, read as two parts: without its paintings, i.e. lacking art

explanation.walkthrough: The National Gallery is London's national collection of paintings; after a robbery it would be without its art.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means free of guile or cunning, which is what naive describes.
